external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of the Wellington LN775 crash at Three Barrows on Dartmoor. The aircraft departed the Overseas Aircraft Dispatch Unit at RAF Hurn, Dorset, on 1 March 1944 for transfer to Mediterranean Air Command en route to Rabat Sale, Morocco, but drifted 25 miles off its briefed route.
external_narratives.key_details: Aircraft flew into the hillside in cloud on a westerly track and burned out. Four crew killed. Wreckage was not located for three days after the crash. Small pieces of melted aluminium and heat-discharged cartridge cases remain at the site.

narrative: Vickers Wellington B Mk X LN775 was lost on 1 March 1944. It belonged to 3 Overseas Aircraft Dispatch Unit at RAF Hurn, Dorset, and was on a transfer flight to Mediterranean Air Command at Rabat, Morocco. It drifted about 25 miles off the briefed route and flew into the hillside at Three Barrows Hill on Dartmoor in cloud. All four crew were killed. Dartmoor Explorations names them as Pilot Officer Frederick Cooke, Flight Sergeants William Jack and Alfred Beeston, and Sergeant John Yeates. Their roles, ages, service numbers and burial places are not yet confirmed from CWGC or IBCC.
community_connection: A temporary memorial at the site lists the four crew. No source found says who looks after it.
